newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle knocked mostly lower by pork complex.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle knocked mostly lower by pork complex.

text.p: CME live cattle futures finished mostly lower on spillover pressure from a drop in pork complex futures and a lack of demand linked to slow cash markets, traders said.

Live cattle ended 0.525 cent a lb lower to up 0.175 with April off most at 68.100 cents and only lightly traded December and February higher. Feeder cattle ended 0.175 cent lower to 0.050 higher with only September up and May off 0.175 at 69.075 cents.
Some of the recent strength in cattle pits had stemmed from a rally in pork and a selloff there weighed on cattle futures much of the session. Sell stops added to the setback, traders said.
"They let the air out of (cattle futures) today as the pork situation gave way," said Dennis Smith, broker with LIT division of First Options.

Cash markets provided little direction with boxed beef showing little price change at noon and feedlot trade remaining quiet. Feedlots and packers remained about $3 apart on bids and offers and trade could remain light ahead of the Easter holiday, traders said. Long liquidation ahead of its spot position next week added to pressure in April.
